one_line_reason: Strong human evidence exists, but it is almost entirely L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA) given to cirrhosis/hepatic-encephalopathy patients, not free ornithine used by general supplement buyers.

selected.population: people with cirrhosis, with or at risk of hepatic encephalopathy
selected.intervention: L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA) vs placebo/no intervention or other active agents (Cochrane systematic review of RCTs)
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (review pools multiple RCT doses/routes)
selected.primary_outcome: hepatic encephalopathy (reversal/prevention) and related mortality/safety outcomes
selected.why_selected: Highest-quality synthesis (Cochrane review) of the core LOLA/HE evidence base, though its abstract as retrieved does not state a bottom-line verdict

selected.population: patients with cirrhosis (minimal or overt hepatic encephalopathy), 384 patients across 6 RCTs
selected.intervention: L-ornithine L-aspartate (oral and intravenous formulations) vs placebo/no intervention
selected.primary_outcome: progression to/reversal of overt hepatic encephalopathy
selected.why_selected: Meta-analysis showing significant reduction in progression to overt HE with LOLA, including an oral-route subgroup

selected.population: patients with cirrhosis and minimal hepatic encephalopathy, 292 patients across 6 RCTs
selected.primary_outcome: reversal of minimal hepatic encephalopathy and progression to overt HE
selected.why_selected: Recent meta-analysis with a clear positive effect estimate, oral subgroup analyzed separately

selected.population: patients with hepatic encephalopathy, 858 patients across 12 RCTs
selected.intervention: L-ornithine L-aspartate combined with lactulose vs lactulose alone
selected.primary_outcome: total effective rate and liver-function markers (AST, ALT, NH3, TBIL)
selected.why_selected: Recent large meta-analysis with positive result, included despite being a combination (LOLA+lactulose) comparison

blockers: All efficacy evidence in the shortlist is in cirrhosis/hepatic-encephalopathy patients, a clinical disease population, not general supplement users

The studied exposure is L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA), a specific salt/combination form often dosed intravenously or as prescription-strength sachets; dose and route may not map to a plain L-ornithine label amount
40370740 evaluates LOLA only as an add-on to lactulose, a combination comparison, not the single ingredient alone

handoff_pmids.note: Systematic review of the safety of oral L-ornithine intake in healthy subjects; establishes a NOAEL and catalogs adverse events, not an efficacy study

excluded_pmids.reason: Reviews aminoglycoside/vancomycin/metronidazole antibiotics for hepatic encephalopathy; L-ornithine L-aspartate is not the intervention studied

Reviews prophylactic therapies (rifaximin, lactulose, LOLA, albumin) post-TIPS; narrative synthesis found LOLA prophylaxis not associated with reduced HE occurrence, but LOLA is one of several agents reviewed, not isolated
Network meta-analysis comparing multiple HE treatments (rifaximin, lactulose, probiotics, LOLA); LOLA is one of several comparators, not the focal single-ingredient evidence
Reviews lactulose management of minimal HE; LOLA appears only as one comparator arm in cited studies
Interventions for childhood apraxia of speech; unrelated to L-ornithine, evidently a mismatched retrieval
Reviews probiotics/synbiotics for hepatic encephalopathy risk factors; L-ornithine-L-aspartate is mentioned only as a comparator treatment, not the studied exposure
